questions.title: Mean and Variance of a Binomial Distribution

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(40, 0.65)$. Find the mean and variance of $X$.

questions.title: Recovering Success Probability from the Mean

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(25, p)$, and it is given that $E(X) = 4$. Find the value of $p$ and hence find $\text{Var}(X)$.

questions.title: Recovering n and p from Both Moments

parts.text: For a binomial random variable $X \sim B(n, p)$, the mean is $12$ and the variance is $7.2$. Find the values of $n$ and $p$.

questions.title: Standard Deviation of a Binomial Model

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(50, 0.18)$. Find the variance and standard deviation of $X$, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Equal Variances for Complementary Binomial Categories

parts.text: Over 36 days, a traveller commutes by train with probability $0.35$ and by bus otherwise, independently each day. Let $T$ be the number of days travelling by train and $U$ be the number of days travelling by bus. Find $\text{Var}(T)$ and $\text{Var}(U)$, and confirm that they are equal.

questions.title: Finding the Second Moment from Binomial Parameters

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(20, 0.4)$. Find the value of $E(X^2)$.
The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(48, 0.25)$. Find $E(X)$ and $\text{Var}(X)$.
Find the standard deviation of $X$.
For a binomial random variable $X \sim B(n, p)$, it is given that the mean is $15$ and the variance is $6$. Find the values of $n$ and $p$.
Using your values from part (a), find $P(X = 16)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Batch Defects: Mean Parameter Recovery and Exact Probability

parts.text: A box contains 24 electronic components. Defective components occur independently, and the mean number of defective components per box is $1.92$. Find the probability $p$ that a component is defective, and find the variance of the number of defective components in a box.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen box contains exactly 2 defective components, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Observed Sample Average and Rescaled Experiment

parts.text: A biased 6-sided die is rolled 30 times in an experiment. The long-run average number of sixes obtained is $5.4$. Estimate the probability $p$ of obtaining a six on a single roll, and find the mean and variance of the number of sixes obtained in a series of 12 rolls.
Find the probability of obtaining at least 2 sixes in 12 rolls of this biased die, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Large-Sample Binomial Moments and Quadratic Payoff

parts.text: In a large certification examination, $64\%$ of candidates pass, independently of each other. A cohort of 100 candidates is selected. Let $X$ be the number of candidates who pass. Find $E(X)$, $\text{Var}(X)$, and the standard deviation of $X$.
The examination board awards a financial bonus $B$ (in dollars) to the testing centre given by $B = 150 + 5X - 0.1X^2$. Find the expected total bonus $E(B)$.

questions.title: Zero-Outcome Identity, Moments, and Standard Deviation Interval

parts.text: A binomial random variable $X \sim B(n, p)$ has mean $E(X) = 18$. It is also given that $P(X = 0) = (0.7)^n$. Find the values of $p$ and $n$.
Find the variance and standard deviation of $X$, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that $X$ lies strictly within one standard deviation of its mean, $P(\mu - \sigma < X < \mu + \sigma)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Two Independent Production Lines: Sum of Moments and Joint Reliability

parts.text: A manufacturing plant has two production lines, $A$ and $B$, operating independently. Line $A$ produces 20 items per hour, with each item having a defective probability of $0.10$. Line $B$ produces 30 items per hour, with each item having a defective probability of $0.15$. Let $T$ be the total number of defective items produced by both lines in an hour ($T = X_A + X_B$). Find $E(T)$ and $\text{Var}(T)$.
Find the standard deviation of the total number of defective items produced in an hour, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that in a randomly chosen hour, Line $A$ produces at most 1 defective item and Line $B$ produces at most 2 defective items.
